content:
**Observations:**
- Affected part: corn stalk (stem), close-up view
- Color: tan/straw-colored, dry, bleached appearance — classic stalk rot coloration
- Key feature: small, discrete diamond/lens-shaped dark brown lesions on the internode surface
- The node area shows some dark discoloration/necrosis
- Stalk appears dry and bleached overall, consistent with late-season stalk rot

**Reasoning:**
The diamond-shaped lesions on the stalk internodes are a hallmark sign of **Diplodia Stalk Rot** (*Stenocarpella maydis*). These characteristic small, diamond/lenticular-shaped marks on the rind of bleached stalks are diagnostic for this disease. Charcoal rot shows black internal discoloration; Gibberella rot shows pink/red coloration; Fusarium shows pinkish discoloration. The external diamond-shaped lesions on a tan, dry stalk point specifically to Diplodia.

The overall bleached appearance and node discoloration are consistent. No pink/red coloration (rules out Gibberella/Fusarium) and no internal black discoloration visible (rules out Charcoal rot)."}
